hero.title: The autonomous engineer that never merges a guess
hero.subtitle: Code Zero reads your pull requests, reproduces the problem, writes the fix, and proves it with a passing run. Observe mode is the default, so nothing touches your repository until you say so.
hero.note: No credit card. Runs on your own infrastructure.

logos.title: Built on the tooling your pipeline already speaks

features.title: Everything between a review comment and a verified fix
features.subtitle: Code Zero is a runtime, not a chat window. Each stage is an explicit state transition you can inspect, replay, and gate.

observe.title: Observe by default
observe.description: Every run starts read-only. Code Zero reports what it found and what it would change; promoting to fix mode is a deliberate, auditable step.

runner.title: One execution boundary
runner.description: Commands and file writes go through a single runner boundary with path validation and escape rejection, so there is exactly one place to audit.

verify.title: Fixes that come with proof
verify.description: A change is only proposed once the repository's own checks pass against it. Failed verification ends the run instead of opening a hopeful pull request.

models.title: Any model provider
models.description: Native OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google adapters, AI Gateway, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The runtime never depends on a specific provider.

sandbox.title: Leased sandboxes
sandbox.description: Hosted execution through a provider-neutral runner pool: every lease has a maximum lifetime, quotas are checked before provisioning, and expired sandboxes are stopped.

policy.title: Policy you keep in git
policy.description: Modes, model selection, and permitted commands live in repository configuration, reviewed like any other change to your codebase.

testimonials.title: What teams do with it
testimonials.subtitle: Code Zero is used where a wrong automated change is expensive.

one.quote: We pointed it at a backlog of stale review comments and let it run in observe mode for a week. It surfaced two real null-dereference paths our linters never flagged.
one.author: Maya Chen

two.quote: The part that sold us was the runner boundary. There is one file to read if you want to know everything the agent is allowed to execute.
two.author: Jonas Weber

three.quote: It never opens a pull request it cannot back with a green run, which means our reviewers stopped treating agent output as noise.
three.author: Amelia Ortiz

faq.title: Questions people ask before the first run
faq.subtitle: Anything else, and the answer is usually in the docs.

write.question: Can Code Zero change my repository without asking?
write.answer: No. Observe mode is the default and never writes to a target repository. Fix mode has to be selected explicitly in repository policy, and every write still goes through the runner boundary.

models.question: Which model providers are supported?
models.answer: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Generative AI natively, plus AI Gateway and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The provider is selected in repository policy and its credential comes from the environment.

selfhost.question: Do I have to use the hosted tiers?
selfhost.answer: No. The runtime is Apache-2.0 licensed and fully functional self-hosted. Paid tiers exist for teams that would rather not operate the sandbox pool themselves.

secrets.question: What happens to my source code and secrets?
secrets.answer: Secrets are never written to logs, prompts, fixtures, or error messages. On self-hosted runs, code never leaves your infrastructure except for the model calls you configure.

cancel.question: Can I cancel or change plan later?
cancel.answer: Yes, at any time and from your own dashboard. Downgrading keeps every run you have already recorded; only retention beyond the new tier's window is dropped.

cta.title: Point it at one pull request
cta.subtitle: Observe mode costs you nothing but a model call, and you will know within one run whether it earns a place in your pipeline.
